title: Deducting Expenses from Assessable Income Tax for Taxi Drivers and Private Hire Car Drivers
what_it_is: Deducting Expenses from Assessable Income Tax for Taxi Drivers and Private Hire Car Drivers

sections.label: Tax deduction for private hire drivers
sections.summary: The Minister explains that private car drivers cannot claim car-related tax deductions, while private hire drivers may claim non-car-related expenses, and says the tax policy is being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) what is the rationale behind allowing taxi drivers but not private hire vehicle drivers to deduct expenses, such as vehicle rental fees, fuel and ERP, from their assessable income tax; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider allowing tax deductibility of these expenses for private hire vehicle drivers based on the mileage clocked on private hire driving.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: It is in support of our long-standing policies on car ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: That is why private car drivers today are not allowed to claim tax deduction on any car-related expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Private hire car drivers can, however, claim tax deduction on non-car-related expenses, such as commissions paid to third-party operators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: With the introduction of private hire car services, the private hire car drivers are essentially operating in the same space as taxis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We have noted the feedback from Members of this House and the National Private Hire Vehicles Association.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We are carefully reviewing this matter to see how we can refine the tax policy to ensure they remain relevant and effective.

sections.label: Review of private hire regulations
sections.summary: MOT and LTA are reviewing how this group of companies should be regulated compared with taxi companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: MOT and Land Transport Authority (LTA) are reviewing the regulations for this group of companies, how they should be regulated vis-a-vis taxi companies.

sections.label: Consistency of tax and regulatory treatment
sections.summary: The Minister says tax treatment must be consistent with regulatory treatment, and both MOT and MOF reviews will be announced once completed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think the tax treatment must be consistent with also the regulatory treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I believe MOT and LTA have announced that they are doing this review on the regulations of private hire car services, and we at the Ministry of Finance (MOF) are also looking at the tax treatment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Once the reviews are completed, we will be able to announce on the MOT side, the regulations; and on the MOF side, the tax treatment.
